levels.name: Attentive Administrator
levels.description: He reads the granary ledgers himself and knows which magistrates are lying. Little escapes him.

levels.name: Steady Governor
levels.description: Years of patient administration have taught him where every denarius hides and every grievance festers.

levels.name: Pillar of the Province
levels.description: Merchants set their scales by his word. Provinces under his hand simply do not go wrong.

levels.name: Distracted
levels.description: Petitions pile up unread while he attends to his hunting dogs. The clerks have noticed.

levels.name: Negligent
levels.description: The city runs itself, badly. Officials skim freely, knowing no audit will ever come.

levels.name: Absent in Spirit
levels.description: He governs the way a shipwreck sails. The people have stopped bringing him their troubles and started solving them with knives.

levels.name: Fair-Dealing
levels.description: He hears both sides before he rules, a habit rare enough to be remarked upon in the market.

levels.name: Just
levels.description: His verdicts are quoted in neighboring towns. Bribes offered to him have a way of ending up as evidence.

levels.name: Incorruptible
levels.description: Men swear oaths on his name as if he were a temple. No purse has ever been found that fits his hand.

levels.name: Grasping
levels.description: Contracts in his district cost a little extra, paid quietly at his back door.

levels.name: Corrupt
levels.description: Justice here is an auction and he is the auctioneer. Honest traders have begun routing around his city.

levels.name: Rotten to the Core
levels.description: He has sold everything but the city walls, and those are under negotiation. His name is a curse in three languages.

levels.name: Stern Assessor
levels.description: He counts olive trees from horseback and taxes accordingly. Nothing is written off.

levels.name: Squeezer of Purses
levels.description: Farmers hide their best amphorae when his collectors ride out. The treasury, at least, is grateful.

levels.name: Bleeder of Provinces
levels.description: It is said he could tax the shade of a fig tree. The revenue is magnificent and the muttering constant.

levels.name: Openhanded
levels.description: He funds a fountain here, a festival there. People wave when his litter passes.

levels.name: Beloved Benefactor
levels.description: His name is carved over a bathhouse he paid for himself. The crowd would carry him to office on their shoulders.

levels.name: Bold
levels.description: When the line wavers he is seen where the spears are thickest, and it steadies men.

levels.name: Brave
levels.description: He has led charges that older officers called suicide, and walked back from each one.

levels.name: Lion of the Line
levels.description: Soldiers boast of serving under him and enemies aim for him first. He would not have it otherwise.

levels.name: Hesitant
levels.description: He gives the order to advance a heartbeat too late, and the men feel that heartbeat.

levels.name: Craven
levels.description: His tent is always pitched nearest the road home. Veterans exchange looks when he speaks of glory.

levels.name: Coward
levels.description: He has survived every defeat he caused, usually at a gallop. Assassins can never quite catch a man this practiced at fleeing.

levels.name: Competent Commander
levels.description: He reads ground the way a scribe reads a ledger, and posts his reserves where they will matter.

levels.name: Skilled Commander
levels.description: His battles tend to be decided before the first javelin flies. Opposing captains have learned to dread his patience.

levels.name: Master of the Field
levels.description: Students of war will argue over his maneuvers for a century. His soldiers simply say the old man does not lose.

levels.name: Uncertain in Command
levels.description: He asks his council what they think, then asks again. Battles rarely wait for a third opinion.

levels.name: Indecisive
levels.description: His orders arrive contradicting his previous orders. The ranks have started obeying whichever came first.

levels.name: Scarred
levels.description: The seam across his jaw ends any argument about whether he has stood in a shield wall.

levels.name: Battle-Worn
levels.description: He carries old iron weather in his bones and the respect of every man who has bled beside him.

levels.name: Iron-Scarred
levels.description: There is more scar than skin on his sword arm. Recruits stare; veterans salute.

levels.name: Wall-Breaker
levels.description: He walks a city's perimeter once and knows where the mortar is old. Gates tend to open for him early.

levels.name: Siege Master
levels.description: Rams, ramps, starvation, treachery — he uses whichever is cheapest. Walls are, to him, a temporary condition.

levels.name: Taker of Towns
levels.description: One captured settlement may be luck. His name now travels ahead of his army.

levels.name: Conqueror
levels.description: Cities he approaches begin negotiating before he arrives. It saves everyone time.

levels.name: Overlord of Provinces
levels.description: Maps must be redrawn because of him. His soldiers follow a legend and know it.

levels.name: Harsh
levels.description: His punishments are exact, public, and remembered. Crime drops; so does laughter.

levels.name: Cruel
levels.description: He makes examples the way other men make speeches. Order holds in his lands the way ice holds a river.

levels.name: The Butcher
levels.description: Whole towns went silent to buy his reputation. Even his allies check the wine, and nobody dares raise a hand against him.

levels.name: Clement
levels.description: He spared a garrison that expected crucifixion. Word of such things spreads faster than armies.

levels.name: Merciful
levels.description: Conquered peoples petition to be governed by him. His enemies call it softness, quietly, from a distance.

levels.name: Dealer in Chains
levels.description: He knows the price of a strong back in every market from here to the coast.

levels.name: Slave Lord
levels.description: His estates run on captive labor and his ledgers run on captive sales. Wealth flows; goodwill does not.

levels.name: Observant
levels.description: He makes the proper offerings on the proper days, and the priests speak well of him.

levels.name: Pious
levels.description: He has paid for altars from his own purse. The devout of the city count him one of their own.

levels.name: Beloved of the Gods
levels.description: Omens read in his presence come out favorable with suspicious regularity. Soldiers touch his cloak before battle.

levels.name: Fond of the Cup
levels.description: Morning audiences have moved to the afternoon, for everyone's comfort.

levels.name: Drunkard
levels.description: He signed a grain contract twice and a marriage contract once, remembering neither. His stewards now hide the seals.

levels.name: Sodden Wreck
levels.description: The wine has finished what ambition started. An assassin would only have to follow the singing.

levels.name: Lettered
levels.description: He can check his own accounts and quote enough verse to survive a dinner party.

levels.name: Learned
levels.description: Geometry, rhetoric, the histories — he has read them and, more unusually, remembers them.

levels.name: Philosopher
levels.description: Scholars travel to argue with him and leave converted. He governs as if administration were a branch of ethics.

levels.name: Clear Speaker
levels.description: When he addresses the assembly, the back rows stop talking. That is rarer than it sounds.

levels.name: Orator
levels.description: He has talked down two riots and talked up one war. Crowds leave his speeches convinced they thought of it themselves.

levels.name: Voice of the Assembly
levels.description: His speeches are copied and sold by weight. Rivals hire men just to cough during them.

levels.name: Listless
levels.description: The army breaks camp at noon because its general breaks fast at eleven.

levels.name: Indolent
levels.description: Opportunities have learned not to wait for him. His couch has a permanent impression.

levels.name: Vigorous
levels.description: He rides the column's length twice a day and wears out younger men's horses doing it.

levels.name: Tireless
levels.description: Dispatches leave his tent at all hours. His enemies' best scouts report that he is, somehow, already here.

levels.name: Keeper of Stores
levels.description: His columns march with full bellies and dry boots, which is most of the art of war.

levels.name: Master of the March
levels.description: He counts wagons the way poets count syllables. His armies arrive early, fed, and irritatingly cheerful.

levels.name: Magistrate's Bearing
levels.description: Office sits on him like a well-cut cloak. Older men have started asking his opinion.

levels.name: Statesman
levels.description: He trades favors the way merchants trade grain, and always at a profit to the state — mostly.

levels.name: Elder of the State
levels.description: Factions that agree on nothing agree to hear him out. His silence in council is itself a form of argument.

levels.name: Self-Assured
levels.description: Confidence this loud is easily mistaken for greatness, and sometimes is.

levels.name: Arrogant
levels.description: He no longer hears advice, only interruptions. Capable men have begun requesting other postings.

levels.name: Insufferable
levels.description: He refers to his victories in the plural and his errors not at all. Allies endure him; subjects merely wait.

levels.name: Shrewd Bargainer
levels.description: He haggles for the city as if the coin were his own, which the merchants find deeply unsettling.

levels.name: Keen Trader
levels.description: He knows the price of tin in three ports and the tides that move it. Caravans reroute to his markets.

levels.name: Merchant Prince
levels.description: Half the harbor owes him money and the other half owes him favors. Trade follows him like gulls follow a fishing boat.

levels.name: Patron of Masons
levels.description: He visits building sites uninvited and asks pointed questions about foundations. The work goes faster when he is near.

levels.name: Master Builder
levels.description: Aqueducts, drains, colonnades — he thinks in stone. Cities in his care visibly outgrow their neighbors.

levels.name: Improving Landlord
levels.description: He walks his fields at dawn and argues with farmers about manure. The harvests take his side.

levels.name: Lord of Acres
levels.description: Under his eye the terraces climb the hills and the granaries need enlarging. Land simply yields more for him.

levels.name: Watchful
levels.description: He sits with his back to the wall and knows every face at his table. Sensible, in these times.

levels.name: Sees Knives Everywhere
levels.description: Three food tasters, locked doors, letters read over a candle. Hard to kill; harder to befriend.

levels.name: Firm Hand
levels.description: Sentries in his camp stay awake. The one who didn't is the reason the rest do.

levels.name: Disciplinarian
levels.description: His men grumble on the drill field and hold like bedrock in battle. They understand the exchange.
